"""Regression tests for boltons.strutils.ordinalize.

A regression made every number whose tens digit is 2 (20-29, 120-129, ...)
return the teen suffix ``th`` and made actual teens (10-19, 110-119, ...)
fall through to the last-digit rule, producing e.g. ``11st`` and ``22th``.

The correct English rules are:
  * 11, 12, 13 (and 111, 112, 113, ...) take ``th``;
  * otherwise the last digit decides: 1 -> st, 2 -> nd, 3 -> rd, else th.
"""

import pytest

from boltons.strutils import ordinalize


ORDINAL_CASES = [
    # single digits
    (1, '1st'),
    (2, '2nd'),
    (3, '3rd'),
    (4, '4th'),
    (5, '5th'),
    (9, '9th'),
    (0, '0th'),
    # teens: always 'th'
    (10, '10th'),
    (11, '11th'),
    (12, '12th'),
    (13, '13th'),
    (14, '14th'),
    (15, '15th'),
    (19, '19th'),
    # twenties: last-digit rule, not the teen rule
    (20, '20th'),
    (21, '21st'),
    (22, '22nd'),
    (23, '23rd'),
    (24, '24th'),
    (25, '25th'),
    (29, '29th'),
    # other tens
    (30, '30th'),
    (31, '31st'),
    (32, '32nd'),
    (33, '33rd'),
    (40, '40th'),
    # hundreds/thousands: same rules repeat
    (100, '100th'),
    (101, '101st'),
    (102, '102nd'),
    (103, '103rd'),
    (110, '110th'),
    (111, '111th'),
    (112, '112th'),
    (113, '113th'),
    (114, '114th'),
    (120, '120th'),
    (121, '121st'),
    (122, '122nd'),
    (123, '123rd'),
    (124, '124th'),
    (1515, '1515th'),
    (3694839230, '3694839230th'),
]

SUFFIX_CASES = [
    (1, 'st'),
    (2, 'nd'),
    (3, 'rd'),
    (4, 'th'),
    (11, 'th'),
    (12, 'th'),
    (13, 'th'),
    (21, 'st'),
    (22, 'nd'),
    (23, 'rd'),
    (24, 'th'),
    (111, 'th'),
    (112, 'th'),
    (113, 'th'),
    (121, 'st'),
    (122, 'nd'),
    (123, 'rd'),
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', ORDINAL_CASES)
def test_ordinalize_number(number, expected):
    assert ordinalize(number) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', SUFFIX_CASES)
def test_ordinalize_ext_only(number, expected):
    assert ordinalize(number, ext_only=True) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', ORDINAL_CASES)
def test_ordinalize_ext_matches_suffix(number, expected):
    # ext_only=True must return exactly the suffix appended by ext_only=False.
    full = ordinalize(number)
    assert full == str(number) + ordinalize(number, ext_only=True)


@pytest.mark.parametrize('text', ['hi', '', 'the 1st', 'hello world', '3rd'])
def test_ordinalize_non_digit_string_unchanged(text):
    # Strings not ending in a digit are returned unchanged, with no suffix.
    assert ordinalize(text) == text
    assert ordinalize(text, ext_only=True) == ''


@pytest.mark.parametrize('number,expected', [
    ('11', '11th'),
    ('12', '12th'),
    ('13', '13th'),
    ('22', '22nd'),
    ('21', '21st'),
    ('23', '23rd'),
    ('122', '122nd'),
    ('1515', '1515th'),
])
def test_ordinalize_numeric_string_input(number, expected):
    # Numeric strings take the same path as ints.
    assert ordinalize(number) == expected
    assert ordinalize(number, ext_only=True) == expected[len(number):]

from boltons.strutils import ordinalize

def ref(n):
    last_two = n % 100
    if 10 <= last_two <= 19:
        suf = 'th'
    else:
        suf = {1: 'st', 2: 'nd', 3: 'rd'}.get(n % 10, 'th')
    return str(n) + suf

bad = [n for n in range(0, 5000) if ordinalize(n) != ref(n)]
# ext_only must equal suffix
bad_ext = [n for n in range(0, 5000) if ordinalize(n, ext_only=True) != ref(n)[len(str(n)):]]
# string passthrough preserved
strings = ['hi', '', 'hello world', 'no digits here', '3rd']
bad_str = [s for s in strings if ordinalize(s) != s or ordinalize(s, ext_only=True) != '']
print('mismatches 0..4999:', len(bad), bad[:5])
print('ext_only mismatches:', len(bad_ext), bad_ext[:5])
print('string passthrough mismatches:', bad_str)
"
